haiku-low.q1: Sign-in still works. The sub is found in user_identities and start_session runs. The new Gmail address is ignored, and users.email is never changed.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter the correct password on the confirm-password page. Only then is the identity inserted, the pending link deleted, and a session started.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds one failure and the page stays without extending the 10 minutes. At 5 failures the account locks for 15 minutes, and the pending link is deleted and the user sent to login.
haiku-low.q4: No matching email: a user is created with no password and verified email, the identity is inserted, and a session starts. Unverified email: refused, pointed to email and password, nothing created.
haiku-low.q5: Both fail with an error page and nothing changes. At 12 minutes the attempt has expired after 10. A second load finds the state already deleted by the first callback.
haiku-low.q6: A new sessions row (14 days) and a new sid cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax) via start_session. Any old sessions row for the existing sid cookie is deleted first.
haiku-low.q7: No password or email match is required. The sid cookie must give a live session for the attempt's user_id. If the sub or user already has a Google link, it is refused.
haiku-low.q8: In the Redis attempt oidc:attempt:<state>, kept 10 minutes. The callback reads and deletes it atomically, and it also expires after 10 minutes.
haiku-low.q9: Redis oidc:pending:<random id> holds the verified sub, the existing user id and next. The browser holds the random id in an HttpOnly cookie. Successful link, account lock, or 10-minute expiry deletes it.
haiku-low.q10: In the PostgreSQL user_identities table. user_id is UNIQUE and google_sub is PRIMARY KEY, which enforce one Google account per user and one user per Google account.
haiku-low.q11: The user is sent back to where they started (login page or settings) with a neutral message. The exchange is not retried; the attempt is gone, so the user starts again.
haiku-low.q12: The mode is stored server-side in the attempt, never taken from the callback request. For link mode, the sid session's user_id must equal the attempt's user_id.

sonnet.q1: Nothing changes: if the sub is in user_identities, start_session is called for that user (landing on next or /home). Email change makes no difference; Google never changes users.email.
sonnet.q2: A pending link is saved (Redis, with next) and a cookie set; the user must enter the existing account's correct password on the confirm page (lockout rules apply). Then the identity is inserted, the pending link deleted, and start_session is called.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins; the page stays and the pending link's 10 minutes is not extended. At 5 failures the account locks for 15 minutes, failed_logins resets to 0, the pending link is deleted and the user is sent to the login page (no link made).
sonnet.q4: Verified and no matching user: create a user with NULL password_hash, email_verified_at now, the ID token email; insert the identity and start_session. Email not verified: refuse, point to email and password, nothing created.
sonnet.q5: Error page and nothing changes: the attempt expired (10 minutes) or was already deleted on first read, so state is unknown/expired/used.
sonnet.q6: The same kind of session as a password login, via start_session: a new sessions row (14 days, sliding) and sid cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax). If the browser sent a sid cookie, the old sessions row is deleted first.
sonnet.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required. If the sub is already linked to anyone (or the user already has a Google account), the link is refused with a message and back to settings; nothing changes.
sonnet.q8: In a Redis attempt entry oidc:attempt:<state> (holding nonce, PKCE verifier, mode, user_id, next). It is removed when the callback reads it (atomic read-and-delete) or by the 10 minute expiry.
sonnet.q9: In Redis entry oidc:pending:<random id>, holding the verified Google sub, the existing user, and next. The browser refers to it by the random id in an HttpOnly cookie. It is deleted on successful link, when the account locks (or is already locked), or by the 10 minute expiry.
sonnet.q10: PostgreSQL table user_identities (user_id, google_sub, created_at). user_id is UNIQUE (one Google account per user, references users with ON DELETE CASCADE) and google_sub is the PRIMARY KEY (one user per Google account).
sonnet.q11: It is treated as a Google error: the user is sent back to the login page or settings with a neutral message, nothing changes. The exchange is not retried (10 second timeout); the attempt is already gone, so the user simply tries again.
sonnet.q12: By the mode stored server-side in the attempt (login or link), never taken from the callback request. For link, the attempt stores user_id; the callback requires the sid cookie to give a live sessions row whose user_id equals the attempt's user_id, otherwise error page and nothing changes.
